newsitem.title: GERMANY: Broker sees lower German spring barley plantings.
newsitem.headline: Broker sees lower German spring barley plantings.

text.p: German spring barley plantings this year may have dropped by five percent from last year's 760,000 hectares, but would still be at historically high levels, specialist broker Jochen Mautner GmbH said.
Mautner, who surveyed acreages and varieties, said last year's area was unusually high because severe damage to winter grains resulted in large spring resowings.
Spring barley sowings took place early this year because of warm weather in March so that 90 percent of field work was complete by April 8, two or three weeks ahead of schedule.
Cold weather in April retarded growth but did not cause any damage.
Spring barley crops may qualify for malting purposes, where prices have been low over the last few months because of low demand, Mautner noted.
Contract negotiations ahead of the harvest have not yielded any results but prices are expected to be below 1996 levels.
Malt prices were also falling because of competition between maltsters and forecasts of declining beer production. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
